label: Decide: Score
description: Ask a decision model where something falls on an ordered scale, and get its position with each level's probability: often cheaper than an LLM and a better fit for rating something (urgency from low to critical, a 1 to 5 rating, how relevant a result is) before an LLM or a person sees it, or after either answers. What it judges is the ports you add, one per piece, each named and typed: `urgency = DecisionScore(ticket: String) { provider: decider.provider, instructions: "How urgent is this ticket?", levels: ["Can wait for the next release", "Should be fixed this week", "Blocking revenue right now"], ticket: inbox.text }`. The values go in one object keyed by port name and each file follows it under its port's name, so the question can point at either (`ticket`, or a nested field as `ticket.messages[0]`). A value (text, a record, a dict, a list of those) is sent as it is, and a file, or a list of files, on a port of its own: a text or JSON file as its content (for anything past a wire's size), an image, audio clip or video as itself (audio and video on cloudflare/clef-omni only). A file inside a record is refused: give it its own port. Write each level as a situation that stands on its own, never "more than the last". To rank several items, score each one (a Loop over them) and sort by `score`.

inputs.name: provider
inputs.description: Which decision model and credential: wire an OpenRouter Decision Model node's `provider`.

inputs.name: instructions
inputs.label: Question
inputs.description: What to place on the scale, with what counts and what only looks like it.

inputs.name: levels
inputs.label: Levels
inputs.description: The scale's levels, lowest first, at least two, each describing a situation that stands alone.

outputs.name: score
outputs.description: The probability-weighted position on the scale, from 0 (the first level) to the number of levels minus 1: 1.99 on three levels is almost all on the last.

outputs.name: level
outputs.description: The most likely level, as written in `levels` (the lower one on a tie).

outputs.name: probabilities
outputs.description: Each level's probability, in the order of `levels`.

outputs.name: confidence
outputs.description: How concentrated the probabilities are on one level, 1 when all of it sits on one. It says nothing about whether the answer is right: use it to send a spread-out answer to a person or a bigger model.

then.message: DecisionScore '{id}' takes, on each added input, exactly one of: a value made of JSON (text, a record, a dict, a list of those), a file, or a list of files, and these are none of those: {names}. Give each file a port of its own (`photo: Image`, `photos: List[Image]`) rather than a field of a record, an item of a list mixed with text, or one type with a value (`String | Image`).
DecisionScore '{id}' has nothing to decide about: add one input for each piece of what the model should judge, named after it and typed, like `DecisionScore(review: String)`.
